title: The many versions of HTTP
description: Thirty years of HTTP, from the first written HTTP/1.0 and 1.1 specifications through the split into parts, to one shared set of semantics over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.
questions: what is the difference between http 1.1 http 2 and http 3
why was http rewritten so many times

steps.title: HTTP/1.0
steps.subtitle: The first written spec
steps.description: RFC 1945 documented what browsers and servers were already doing in the mid-1990s. It is Informational, not a standard.

steps.title: HTTP/1.1 arrives
steps.subtitle: Persistent connections
steps.description: HTTP/1.1 added persistent connections, chunked transfer and better caching. The first version was superseded within two years by the revision that stayed in use for fifteen.

steps.title: Split into parts
steps.description: RFC 2616 was split into six documents covering messaging, semantics, conditional requests, ranges, caching and authentication. All six have since been replaced.

steps.title: One semantics, three syntaxes
steps.description: The HTTP meaning of methods, status codes and header fields now lives in one document that every version of HTTP shares. HTTP caching and HTTP/1.1 messaging have their own documents.

steps.title: HTTP/2
steps.subtitle: Multiplexing
steps.description: HTTP/2 puts requests in binary frames and multiplexes them on one TCP connection, with header compression (HPACK). RFC 7540 was replaced by RFC 9113 in 2022.

steps.title: HTTP/3 and QUIC
steps.subtitle: Over UDP
steps.description: HTTP/3 maps HTTP onto QUIC, a UDP-based transport with built-in encryption, so one lost packet no longer stalls every stream.
